title: Cryptococcus neoformans adapts to host CO2 concentrations via metabolic and stress-response remodeling
experiments_summary:
1. Genome-wide competitive fitness screen: 4,692 deletion mutants from the Madhani C. neoformans library (KN99α background) were each co-cultured 1:1 with mNeonGreen-labeled H99 reference strain in 96-well plates in RPMI/MOPS at 37°C for 24h in ambient air or 5% CO2; strain ratios were quantified by flow cytometry to calculate competitive fitness indices (3 replicates, Student t-test, P<0.05, ±0.2 cutoff). GO term enrichment analysis was performed on genes with altered fitness.

2. HOG pathway activation assay: H99 cells were grown on RPMI agar plates, shifted to 5% CO2 or ambient air for 2h, lysed in NaOH, and immunoblotted using anti-Hog1 and anti-phospho-p38 antibodies to assess Hog1 phosphorylation status.

3. ESCRT/VPS mutant CO2 fitness and pH sensitivity: Selected VPS deletion mutants were tested by competitive fitness assay in 5% CO2, and by serial dilution spot assay on YPD plates adjusted to pH 8, to distinguish CO2-specific from pH-related phenotypes.

4. PKA-Rim101 pathway epistasis: A rim101Ser773Ala phosphosite mutant strain (provided by O'Meara lab) was tested by competitive fitness assay at 5% CO2 alongside pka1∆ and pkr1∆ mutants to assess independence of PKA and Rim101 pathways in CO2 tolerance.

5. Sphingolipid biosynthesis assays: The gcs1∆ mutant was tested by competitive fitness assay at 5% CO2. IPC synthase inhibitor aureobasidin A was applied as a disk diffusion assay on RPMI lawns of H99 incubated at 37°C in ambient or 5% CO2 for 48h to assess IPC branch requirement.

6. UPR pathway mutant fitness: ire1∆ and hxl1∆ mutants were tested by competitive fitness assay at 5% CO2.

7. Non-lipid untargeted metabolomics: H99 cells were grown in RPMI/MOPS at 37°C for 24h in ambient or 5% CO2 (4 biological replicates per condition). Metabolites were extracted by chloroform-methanol-water liquid-liquid extraction and analyzed by HILIC-UHPLC-MS/MS (HESI, positive and negative polarity). Data were processed in Compound Discoverer 3.2 with median-centering normalization, and differential features identified by Welch-corrected two-tailed t-test (log2 FC>1, P<0.05).

8. Glucose supplementation growth assay: H99 was grown in RPMI/MOPS supplemented with 0.2%, 2%, 5%, or 10% glucose at 37°C for 48h in ambient or 5% CO2; final cell densities were measured.

9. UXS1 and UGE1 mutant fitness: uxs1∆ and uge1∆ competitive fitness was measured at 5% CO2 by flow cytometry-based competitive assay.

10. V-ATPase mutant fitness: Multiple mutants lacking V-ATPase subunit or assembly genes were tested by competitive fitness assay at 5% CO2.

11. Urea cycle metabolite quantification: Citrulline and argininosuccinic acid levels were quantified from the metabolomics dataset comparing ambient vs. 5% CO2 conditions.

12. Mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1 staining): H99 cells were grown in 6-well plates in RPMI/MOPS at 37°C for 24h in ambient or 5% CO2, stained with 2.5 µM JC-1 for 1h, and analyzed by flow cytometry (BL2/BL1 MFI ratio).

13. NAD+/NADH and NADP+/NADPH ratio measurements: H99 cells grown under ambient or 5% CO2 for 24h were pelleted, lyophilized, and assayed using commercial colorimetric kits (BioAssay Systems) in biological triplicate.

14. Beta-oxidation and acetyl-CoA pathway mutant fitness: acs1∆, kbc1∆, and acs1∆ kbc1∆ double mutants were tested by competitive fitness assay at 5% CO2.

15. Mouse infection competitive fitness assays: CD1 female mice were infected by intranasal inoculation (5×10^4 CFU, day 10 harvest) or intravenous inoculation (1×10^5 CFU, day 4 harvest) with 1:1 mixtures of H99 and either acl1∆ or yhm2∆ mutants. Lung and brain fungal burdens were quantified by plating on YNB and YNB+hygromycin.

16. Glutathione/cysteine pathway mutant fitness and ROS measurements: gsh1∆, gsh2∆, and sulfur assimilation pathway mutants were tested by competitive fitness assay with or without supplementation of 200 µM cysteine or 1 mM glutathione. ROS levels were measured in WT and gsh2∆ cells grown in ambient or 5% CO2 using 16 µM DCFDA staining and flow cytometry.

17. TOR-Ypk1 pathway ROS measurements: ROS levels were measured by DCFDA assay in ypk1∆ and gcs1∆ mutants compared to WT under ambient and 5% CO2 conditions.

18. Generation of independent yhm2∆ strain: CRISPR/Cas9 SAH and TRACE methods were used to replace the YHM2 ORF with a hygromycin resistance cassette in H99; transformants were verified by PCR at 5' and 3' flanks and for loss of the native locus.
